title: Jude and the Wolf
premise: Juniper Thackeray, gatekeeper and ledger-keeper of the Guild of Impossible Things, discovers that a feral child who speaks the First Tongue is the living seal of an ancient covenant between the human realms and the wolf-kind beyond the gate. When Guildmaster Veyra, secretly the usurper's agent, moves to break the covenant and harvest the gate's power for her armies, Juniper must choose between his sworn duty to the Guild and the truth the child's presence reveals. Hunted through the free cities with the wolf-warden Sable — bound to him by an oath older than either of them — Juniper learns the covenant was never broken by wolves but betrayed by men. In the end, he reforges the covenant at terrible cost, sealing the gate from within while sending the child through to safety, and chooses exile among the wolves over a home that demanded his silence.
about_author: Yara Montrose is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval trade ledgers before turning to fantasy. She writes about doors, debts, and the people paid to keep both shut.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Impossibilities
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. A quiet night at the Guildhouse: Juniper balances impossible accounts, catalogs a bottled echo, and notes the gate's wards humming out of rhythm. Emotional beat: restless unease beneath routine, foreshadowing that something on the other side is counting back.

chapters.title: A Child at the Door
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. During a storm, a mud-caked boy arrives speaking the First Tongue, and every ward on the gate flares in recognition. The Guild orders him held for study; Juniper alone understands fragments of what the child says. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness awakening duty's first crack.

chapters.title: What the Wards Remember
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Deciphering the child's words, Juniper finds matching phrases in the oldest covenant ledger — pages Veyra has ordered sealed. He copies them in secret. Emotional beat: the thrill and guilt of forbidden knowledge.

chapters.title: Sable at the Threshold
chapters.summary: POV Sable. A wolf-warden crosses to the near side under truce, seeking the child she calls Seal-Bearer. She and Juniper clash, then recognize each other as keepers of half a truth. Emotional beat: wary mutual respect kindling into something warmer.

chapters.title: The Guildmaster's Summons
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Veyra interrogates Juniper about the missing pages, offering promotion and warning of the usurper's armies massing beyond the free cities. He lies to her face for the first time. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: First Tongue, First Lessons
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Teaching the child — named Ash — basic speech, Juniper learns the covenant's terms: a life freely given each generation to hold the gate. Ash believes he was sent willingly. Emotional beat: protective love hardening against a fate written for a child.

chapters.title: The Night Market of Borrowed Things
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Seeking allies, Sable trades a memory at the free cities' night market and learns Veyra has bought every record of the last covenant renewal. Emotional beat: loneliness eased by discovering Juniper kept duplicates.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Lies
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Comparing copies, Juniper proves the last renewal never happened — the previous keeper falsified it, and the gate has been running on borrowed time for sixty years. Emotional beat: horror that his own office is built on betrayal.

chapters.title: Veyra's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Veyra. The Guildmaster meets a usurper's envoy: deliver the Seal-Bearer and the gate's power, and the free cities will be spared. She hesitates only over Juniper's usefulness. Emotional beat: cold ambition masking old affection.

chapters.title: Running the Rooftops
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Warned by a sympathetic clerk, Juniper flees with Ash through the city as Guild hunters close in; Sable extracts them across the river. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into exhilaration — he has chosen his side.

chapters.title: The Free Cities Weigh Their Walls
chapters.summary: POV Sable. The fugitives petition the Council of Free Cities, which debates surrendering Ash to buy peace. Juniper argues justice outside the law; the council abstains. Emotional beat: bitter clarity that institutions will not save the innocent.

chapters.title: Ash's Story
chapters.summary: POV Ash (rendered through Juniper's translation). Ash recounts his village's sacrifice rite and how the wolves smuggled him out rather than let him die. Emotional beat: grief met with fierce, family-forged loyalty.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Following ledger clues to a ruined waystation, they find proof the original betrayer was a Thackeray — Juniper's own ancestor. Emotional beat: shame transformed into determination to end a family debt.

chapters.title: Hunters in the Pinewood
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Guild hunters and usurper outriders corner the group; Sable is gravely wounded holding the rearguard. Juniper uses guild-craft to turn the forest itself against their pursuers. Emotional beat: love confessed in blood and adrenaline.

chapters.title: The Covenant's True Terms
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Reading the full original text, Juniper learns the covenant demands not a death but a willing keeping — a soul to hold the gate from inside, alive, aware. Veyra's plan would enslave such a keeper forever. Emotional beat: dread and strange relief entwined.

chapters.title: Armies on the March
chapters.summary: POV Veyra. The usurper's vanguard burns a border town when the council stalls; Veyra, committed now, leads Guild forces to seize Ash. Emotional beat: the point of no return, ambition curdling into ruthlessness.

chapters.title: The Siege of the Gatehouse
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. The trio races to reach the gate before Veyra; a running battle through the Guildhouse ends with Sable captured and Ash cornered. Emotional beat: desperation, sacrifice, and Juniper's refusal to bargain with Veyra even to save Sable.

chapters.title: What Wolves Owe
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Imprisoned, Sable bargains with a conflicted hunter and escapes as wolf-kind masses at the gate for war. Emotional beat: loyalty tested between her pack and the man on the wrong side of the door.

chapters.title: The Breaking Point
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. At the gate, Veyra forces Ash toward the threshold to bind him as an enslaved keeper; Juniper intervenes, revealing the falsified ledgers publicly. Guild ranks fracture. Emotional beat: truth wielded like a blade, love against duty made literal.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. To stop both armies, Juniper speaks the covenant in the First Tongue and offers himself as the willing keeper, stepping through as the gate seals — sparing Ash and shattering Veyra's claim. Emotional beat: grief, awe, and perfect agency in sacrifice.

chapters.title: Aftermath of the Keeping
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Veyra falls to her own faction; the free cities and wolf-kind sign a true accord. Sable refuses to accept the gate as closed and petitions the new covenant for visitation rights. Emotional beat: mourning braided with stubborn hope.

chapters.title: The Keeper Within
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. On the far side, Juniper tends the gate's living heart, visited by Ash and granted one dusk each year when the wards thin and Sable may cross. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace — exile chosen, love sustained, the debt of his name finally paid.
